findings.title: The two `link` arms that round 2's fix ADDED are the only two predicates in the file that are still unfalsifiable, and the row substitutes a different six while keeping the count
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, two mutations, each applied alone to the staged bytes and each leaving `./gradlew :sequencer:test` at 178 tests / BUILD SUCCESSFUL. (a) Delete the four lines `if (entries.stream().anyMatch(e -> e instanceof CommitDelta)) { found.add(new Violation("link", ... "but never wrote a CONTINUE, so its offsets rest on nothing")); }` at Invariants.java:188-191 -> whole sequencer suite green. (b) Delete the five lines `long ancestor = firstAncestorWithDeltas(...); if (ancestor > 0) { found.add(new Violation("link", ... "claims no predecessor, but epoch " + ancestor + " carries committed deltas")); }` at Invariants.java:201-205 -> whole sequencer suite green. Equivalently, `firstAncestorWithDeltas` (17 lines including javadoc, whose sole caller is that arm) can be reduced to `return 0;` and nothing notices. Both arms DO work -- a throwaway probe built each shape and each fired: a chain whose slot 0 is a CommitDelta returns `[link: epoch 1 carries committed deltas but never wrote a CONTINUE]`, and an epoch-2 chain opening with `Continue(0, 0, 0)` above a sealed epoch 1 that assigned 0..4 returns `[link: epoch 2 claims no predecessor, but epoch 1 carries committed deltas]`. So the fixtures are cheap and simply were not written. WHY THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: the second arm is the fix for round 2's blocking finding, quoted in the row itself -- 'a chain that omits or DISOWNS its link was still believed, so `open(0, 0)` reported 0 violating seeds over 240 chains'. Shipping it deletable-with-the-suite-green means the fix for the defect that caused the split is itself unpinned, which is the exact shape of `crossEpochOffsetsChecked()` that this same commit deletes for being a claim that cannot go false. The class javadoc at Invariants.java:32-34 leans on it explicitly -- '`link` -- the only arm that catches either defect this class was split out of M4.12 for' -- a load-bearing claim over code no test can break. AND THE ROW MISDESCRIBES THE COMMIT: backlog.md:266 retains verbatim the sentence naming the deliverable -- 'four predicates the round-1 fix introduced -- the `gap` arm, the `continuedAt` mismatch arm, the never-opened walk-back ... and the seal-bounded `upTo` fold -- each survive deletion with the whole suite green, plus the two arms round 2's fix adds' -- and then appends '⚠️ DELIVERED. Six predicates are now falsifiable' enumerating gap, the I2 one-record boundary, the walk-back, the fold in BOTH directions, and the `continuedAt` fork arm. The COUNT matches the row's 'the count is the argument'; the SET does not: the two round-2 arms are replaced by the I2 boundary (a separate item later in the same row) and by counting the fold twice. Neither replaced arm is deferred anywhere -- M4.22 is the observability accessor, M4.23 is the unsealed-ancestor blind spot plus the empty-chain early return plus the depth cap, M4.24 is the O(E^2) cost, and none of the three mentions either arm. So two of the six named deliverables are undelivered, unpinned and untracked, in a row marked **done**. For contrast, everything else in the file IS individually falsifiable -- measured, one mutation each, one failing fixture each: the fold's `break` at :240 (fails theFOLDStopsAtTheFIRSTSealEvenWhenTheLINKIsWellFormed and aSECONDSealPastAFencedWritersDeltaDoesNOTMoveTheBarrier), checkLink's `break` at :307 (fails the same two, via the `link` arm rather than the `resumes at 8` detail arm, so both arms are genuinely pinned SEPARATELY as the row claims), dropping the whole `upTo` seal scan, deleting the `gap` else-if, `< from` -> `< from - 1`, deleting the I1 arm, deleting the `chain` arm, deleting the `closing == null` arm, deleting the `continuedAt` arm, deleting the `prevSeq` arm, deleting the never-opened while-loop, and gutting `neverOpened` to `entries.isEmpty()`. Minimum fix: two fixtures -- a chain whose first entry is a CommitDelta, and a later chain opening `Continue(0, 0, 0)` above a predecessor that committed -- or, if they are to be deferred, a row that says so and a row text at :266 whose six are the six it delivers.

findings.title: M4.23's measured evidence does not reproduce against the bytes M4.19 ships, because M4.19 withdrew the early return that produced it
findings.failure_scenario: M4.23 states 'Measured: epoch 1 with a delta and NO seal, epoch 2 absent, epoch 3 continuing from 2 and resuming correctly, reports no violations at all.' Probed against the staged bytes (epoch 1 = Continue(0,0,0), delta(1,3,0), no seal; epoch 2 absent; epoch 3 = Continue(0,2,0), delta(1,2,3)): `Invariants.checkChain` returns exactly ONE violation -- `link: epoch 3 continues from epoch 2, which is NOT SEALED -- its writer met no barrier` -- because the same commit withdrew the empty-named-chain early return, so an ABSENT named epoch now reports NOT SEALED. The mechanism the row names IS real and IS reproducible, just with a different fixture: with epoch 2 present-but-never-opened (a single `Seal(0, 3)` at slot 0) above the same unsealed epoch 1, `checkChain(store, prefix, 3)` returns `[]`, so the unsealed ancestor the walk-back actually inherits from is invisible. Consequence if unfixed: an author picking up M4.23 builds the shape the row records, sees a violation, and either concludes the defect is already closed or spends the round rediscovering that the shape is wrong. Minimum fix: change 'epoch 2 absent' to 'epoch 2 present but never opened (a SEAL at slot 0)' in that sentence, since that is the shape that still reports nothing.
